critical_code_review_comments: Login.js:35 uses window.location.search to read the redirect param instead of useLocation/useSearchParams from react-router. Works today but breaks if the route is ever rendered via SSR / a memory router. Prefer `const [params] = useSearchParams(); params.get('redirect')`.

Login.js: the redirect target is taken from a query param and used directly with navigate(). There is no allowlist — an attacker can craft /connexion?redirect=https://evil.tld and after login navigate(...) will treat it as an internal path (which actually neutralises external URLs in react-router), but a relative-but-unintended path is still possible. Consider whitelisting allowed redirect prefixes.

Premium.js:147 — `const isPremium = status?.is_premium || user?.is_premium;` mixes two sources of truth. If `user.is_premium` is stale (cached AuthContext) while `status` says false, the badge will still render. Prefer trusting only the freshly-fetched `status` once it has loaded, or invalidate user.is_premium on status fetch.
Premium.js:109 — the status fetch has empty .catch(() => {}); silently swallows errors. Add a setErr or at least console.warn so prod outages are observable in Sentry/logs.

Premium.js:222 free-card CTA navigates to /mon-profil when authenticated; check if the route is /mon-compte (consistent with Login redirect) — there may be a mismatch (`/mon-profil` vs `/mon-compte`).

services/premium_subscription.py:111 — create_billing_portal creates a Stripe portal session for *any* user that has a stripe_customer_id, even if their current premium_status is 'free' or expired. That means a previously-premium user can still open a portal long after cancellation. Today the portal will just show an inactive subscription, but consider also checking `premium_status in ('active','trialing')`.

rca of the issue: BUG 1 root cause (pre-fix): Login.js used `navigate('/tarot')` hard-coded after login (legacy from oracle funnel). Fix swapped to `navigate(redirect || '/mon-compte')` with redirect read from URLSearchParams. BUG 2 root cause (pre-fix): Premium.js unconditionally rendered the manage-subscription-btn whenever the user was premium; clicking it called POST /api/premium/portal which legitimately 404'd for manual grants (no stripe_customer_id), surfacing as a Stripe 404 in the UI. Fix: gated the manage button behind `!!status?.subscription_id` and show a French explanatory note instead. Both root causes are correctly addressed.
